subject.title: [Bug]: xAI/Grok "could not decrypt encrypted_content" 400 trips the per-model circuit breaker (no auto-recovery)

question: Should maintainers accept source-level reproduction plus redacted pre-fix xAI production logs as sufficient proof for the linked PR's provider-side, non-client-inducible retry trigger?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible, but the live after-fix event requires an organic xAI snapshot/key rotation, so automation cannot safely settle proof sufficiency for the linked PR.

options.title: Accept bounded proof and review the PR
options.body: Treat the pre-fix logs, source-level BadRequestError test shape, and positive/negative predicate coverage as sufficient for this rare provider-side trigger, then continue normal review of the linked fix PR.

options.title: Wait for organic after-fix proof
options.body: Keep the linked PR blocked until a real redacted xAI/Grok gateway retry succeeds after a future provider rotation event.

options.title: Request a broader breaker policy design
options.body: Pause the narrow fix and ask for a larger provider-error-classification design, accepting continued exposure to this specific outage class while that design is scoped.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded proof and review the PR
recommendation.body: Treat the pre-fix logs, source-level BadRequestError test shape, and positive/negative predicate coverage as sufficient for this rare provider-side trigger, then continue normal review of the linked fix PR.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the closest merged recovery behavior in the same predicate/test area and can judge whether the narrow proof is enough for that recovery class.
